gaps.observed: Every phase elides the response mid-object with an ellipsis: the take phase prints one line reading id T-auth-0, status in_progress, then the ellipsis, so the reader never sees what the command actually returns. The object is also hand-wrapped with two keys on one line, which is not how the CLI or JSON.stringify prints it.
gaps.expected: A complete, truthfully formatted response with one key per line and no elision, so the reader can see what take and accept actually return.

gaps.observed: Three beats swap every 2.9s, 3.8s and 5.1s in an 11.7s loop, measured over 30s with zero variance. Each beat carries 11 to 16 words of caption plus a command, a JSON body, a log row, four graph nodes and three counters. The loop also resets to the starting state, so the story never completes on screen.
gaps.expected: A reader who arrives at any moment can read a complete example at their own pace: much slower beats, a progression that accumulates instead of resetting, and a pause control that actually holds a beat.

gaps.selector: figure.landing-panel ul li (pills), figure.landing-panel ol li span (stepper), figure.landing-panel ul.mt-1.5 (log rows), figure.landing-panel pre (json), p.text-13 (caption)
gaps.observed: Nearly all text is below the page's reading size: pills 10.5px, stepper labels 10.5px, log rows 11px, log label 11.5px, header command 11.5 to 12px, JSON 12px, and the caption 13px. The satisfied-when table immediately below the panel renders at 14px and is far easier to read.
gaps.expected: A legible type ramp for a hero, with nothing below 12px, the caption clearly the largest body text in the panel, and the panel reading as comfortably as the table below it.

gaps.selector: figure.landing-panel svg (DAG) and the nested gate card G-auth-prod
gaps.observed: G-auth-prod is drawn inside the card of the task it blocks, so blocking reads as containment. Together with the two connector arrows the relationship is ambiguous, and the inner card shares the outer card's left edge.
gaps.expected: The gate reads as a dependency of T-auth-2, not as its child: a clear visual distinction between task cards and the gate, and an edge treatment that matches what the satisfied-when table below says about BLOCKS.

gaps.observed: A 1152x385 letterbox with large dead areas: the JSON occupies 106px of a 188px pane, the log block ends after one row and leaves the rest of its 101px empty, and the 181px DAG is centred inside a 289px column. The proportion is 3 to 1, which is what makes the whole thing feel cramped and empty at once.
gaps.expected: Proportions that give the example room to breathe, no large empty runs inside a pane, and a height that grows with the content instead of padding it.

gaps.observed: At 390x844 the header drops the framing command completely: the reader sees only rev 5 plus the two icon buttons and the three counters, with no statement of what produced the graph below.
gaps.expected: The command that frames the example is visible on mobile too, or the panel states in plain words what it is showing.

gaps.observed: take, submit and accept are stretched into three 354px cells joined by hairlines, with the active stage marked only by colour. It reads as a progress bar, and the words are not labelled as lifecycle stages.
gaps.expected: Reads as the lifecycle the captions describe, with the current stage unmistakable and the labels legible.
